# Housing gap {#sec-gaps}

<!-- Purpose: the affordable-and-available rental gap by AMI (PUMS, NLIHC-style), the
     starter-home gap (renters who could buy), and minimum income for homeownership by
     price/size/type vs household income profiles. Theme-based takeaway H2s; static ggplot
     only; "Since 2022" callout per section; fig-alt throughout. Built in Task 10. -->



This section quantifies the region's housing shortfall three ways: rental units affordable and available by income band, renters positioned to become owners, and the income required to buy at today's prices.

## How large is the affordable-and-available rental gap by income band?

::: {.callout-note title="To be added"}
An NLIHC-style bar chart of the surplus or deficit of rental units that are both affordable to and available to each AMI band (30/50/80/100/120% AMI), for the region's core three localities (Chesterfield, Henrico, Richmond city). Built from detailed Census microdata, with AMI bands assigned from HUD's FY2026 Income Limits by household size.
:::

## Where along the income spectrum do renters compete for the same units?

::: {.callout-note title="To be added"}
A table of renter households versus affordable units versus affordable-and-available units by AMI band, showing how higher-income occupancy of low-cost units compounds the shortage at the bottom. Source: detailed Census microdata with HUD's FY2026 Income Limits.
:::

## How many renter households could afford to buy a starter home?

::: {.callout-note title="To be added"}
The starter-home gap: renter households whose income supports a mortgage on an entry-level home (payment at or below 28% of monthly income) against the supply of entry-level for-sale units. Sources: Census microdata income distribution, MLS entry-level inventory, and current mortgage rates.
:::

## What income does homeownership require by price point, unit size, and type?

::: {.callout-note title="To be added"}
A minimum-income table (or heat-style chart) by representative price point, unit size, and structure type — down-payment, rate, tax, and insurance assumptions documented in @sec-data-notes — set against the region's household-income distribution to show how many households can afford each segment. Sources: Census microdata and Freddie Mac mortgage rates.
:::

The per-section "Since 2022" comparison: this cycle's gap counts against the 2022 Framework's published gap figures, with the vintage-shift caveat stated alongside. Deltas are narrative, never a validation gate.
